t.d: Terracotta pots, basins and bricks made from the iron-rich clay of Impruneta south of Florence.
t.tech: Clay worked by hand (colombino coiling for large pots) and kiln-fired
t.auth: Frost-resistant iron-rich clay; large pots hand-coiled rather than moulded

t.d: Village pottery tradition making large storage jars (pitharia) and other earthenware.
t.tech: Team throwing of large jars, historically on the migratory summer Ventema campaign

t.d: Stoneware centre best known for red shudei kyusu.

t.p: Song dynasty clay mining; teapots from Ming dynasty–present
t.d: Unglazed stoneware of purple, red and beige Yixing clays, best known for teapots and other teaware.
t.tech: slab-built, coiled, thrown or slip-cast; usually unglazed, fired 1100–1200 °C
t.mat: zisha (zi ni), zhu ni, duan ni clays
t.auth: clay colour and texture; potter's seal on base (widely imitated since the 17th century)

t.d: Hard white charcoal from ubame oak, prized for long, clean, hot burning in Japanese grilling.
t.tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), then about 1,000 °C, cured in damp earth, sand and ash
t.auth: Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative yellow label; regional collective trademark since 2006; metallic ring when struck

t.d: Free-forged "blue" Austrian scythe blades, exported worldwide in many market-specific forms; Austrian intangible cultural heritage since 2014.
t.tech: free-form forging and spreading of the blade under water-driven hammers
t.mat: steel; charcoal and later mineral coal
t.auth: guild and master marks that became trade marks; about 215 works in 11 guilds c. 1800, two makers left

t.p: Edo period to present; designated traditional craft 1996
t.d: Forged-blade craft of Miki, which grew from carpenters' tools made to rebuild the town after Miki Castle fell to Hideyoshi.
t.tech: Iron and carbon steel forge-welded by hammering, mud-coated hardening, hand sharpening and finishing
ctr: Miki Industrial Cooperative Association, Miki City
t.auth: Traditional craft mark of the designated production area (Miki City)

t.d: Up to about 200 regional billhook shapes made by local and Midlands edge-tool works for hedging and coppice work.
t.auth: maker stamp and regional pattern name

t.p: Middle Ages to present; designated traditional craft 2009
t.d: Sanjo forged blades, grown from medieval sickles and hoes into knives, chisels, axes and wood shears.
t.tech: Free forging, iron and carbon steel forge-welded, mud-coated hardening, all finishing by hand
ctr: Echigo Sanjo Blacksmith Group, Sanjo Blacksmithing Dojo
t.auth: Traditional craft mark of the designated production area (Sanjo City)
